newsitem.title: USA: DataMark to link online service with TV.
newsitem.headline: DataMark to link online service with TV.

text.p: DataMark Holding Inc said Tuesday it plans to offer an Internet service that will post news generated by local television affiliates as well as a mix of local and national advertising.
The service, called WorldNow Online Network, is to be launched in April.
WorldNow president Stanton Jones said the concept is born out the belief that local television stations are interested in doing more via the Internet, but lack the expertise.
"Broadcast stations right now are in a quandary. ... They all know they should be doing something," Jones said in an interview with Reuters. "We give them a boilerplate."
WorldNow will provide computer users with local and national advertising, promotions, news, information and entertainment. It also will offer e-mail and Internet access.

The company said WorldNow has commitments with television stations in the top 50 markets and is in contract negotiations with more than 25 other stations. It said that as many as 100 broadcast affiliates are expected to sign on as part of the network by the end of this year.
The local news feeds offered by the television stations will be a combination of text, still photographs, audio and some video.
"We come to them with a turnkey package," Jones said.
WorldNow said the venture will generate revenue from three sources, advertising, fees from the television affiliates and access fees paid by computer users.
Jones said the company expects to have revenue projections for the venture available in the next several weeks.

"The localizing and customizing options will allow advertisers to create highly targeted and effective promotional advertising based on consumer preferences and geographic location," DataMark chief executive Chad Evans said in a statement.
((-- Lisa Marie Pane, New York newsdesk 212-859-1713))
